title: Jamie Dimon tells AI companies to stop fighting data center opposition: 'Build them where they're wanted'
source_used: Moneywise, read on the Yahoo Finance copy; quotes from a Bloomberg News interview
key_facts: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon told Bloomberg News in an interview on 7 Oct 2026 that data centres should be built 'where they wanted'.
He said that in Texas and Virginia people do not want the new data centres and that 'You're not going to win'.
He said companies must be good community citizens and that many are making commitments not to raise consumer electricity costs.
Data centres are a political flashpoint ahead of the November midterms; a Pew poll published 22 Sep 2026 found 50% of Americans say they hurt home energy costs and 54% say they hurt the environment.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on 2 Sep that the industry had done a 'terrible job' of explaining itself, as hyperscalers carry out a $700 billion AI construction spree.
Dimon said AI will 'cure a lot of diseases' but that the agent risks 'are a legitimate concern'.
quote_evidence: "Data centers — build them where they wanted," Dimon told Bloomberg News in an interview on Oct. 7. "Half of the new ones in America, in Texas and Virginia, people don't want them there. You're not going to win."

According to a Pew Research Center poll published on Sept. 22, 50% of Americans said data centers had a negative effect on home energy costs, while 54% said the same about the impact on the environment.
"I do think it'll cure a lot of diseases, and it'll save accidents on the road…It'll make life unbelievable for people," he told Bloomberg.
why_it_matters_hint: A leading banker tells AI firms that fighting local opposition to data centres is a losing battle.
event_date: 7 Oct 2026 (Bloomberg News interview); Moneywise published 10 Oct 2026
notes: Yahoo Finance says the article first appeared on Moneywise; the Moneywise page returned 403 here. The interview was already reported by other outlets on 8 Oct (Times of India, Firstpost, NewsBytes headlines seen). Re-dated, three days old.
